title: Internal secretions and other substances accelerate growth and alter proportions

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Internal secretions and other substances accelerate growth and alter proportions

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Substances inside and outside the organism, such as thyroid and pituitary secretions or iodine compounds, can accelerate growth in a way that changes not only the size but the form or proportions of the organism.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. III: The Rate of Growth

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: We may take it, then, as an established fact, whose full extent and bearings are still awaiting investigation, that there exist substances both within and without the organism which have a marvellous power of accelerating growth, and of doing so in such a way as to affect not only the size but the form or proportions of the organism.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter III, “The Rate of Growth”; topic “Growth and catalytic action”. Scope: animals (tadpoles, mammals, birds), with parallels in plants

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch03-28: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.74

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Controlled perturbations make the causal statement directly testable, and many relevant studies have public data. Coverage is nevertheless uneven, so existing datasets can establish examples rather than fully resolve the broad generalization.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare growth rate, final size, and body-part proportions between hormone or iodine perturbations and matched controls. Support requires accelerated growth accompanied by a statistically detectable allometric or shape change, not size alone.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The claim combines many substances and animal groups.

Phenotype measurements and treatment doses are heterogeneous.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.75
discriminating power: 0.8
data adequacy: 0.6
operationalizability: 0.85
analysis feasibility: 0.7

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is existential: some internal and external substances accelerate growth and change proportions. Mouse endocrine-pathway knockouts, with open body-size and body-composition measures, are enough to confirm or fail that existence claim for internal secretions. External dosing and non-mammal examples remain scattered in papers, which limits scope but does not block a decision on the core assertion.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare body size and body-proportion phenotypes of animals in which thyroid, pituitary or growth-hormone pathways are disrupted with matched controls. A change in both scale and proportions would confirm that such substances can alter form; size changes that are pure scaling, or no growth effect at all, would count against the claim as stated.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Some proportion shifts are secondary to illness rather than a specific growth stimulus.

The open screen is a mouse knockout panel, so tadpoles, birds and external doses such as iodine are outside it.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.65
discriminating power: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.75
operationalizability: 0.75
data existence: 0.8
